# ASP.NET Core + React (Details)

- [ASP.NET Core + React](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/javascript/tutorial-asp-net-core-with-react?view=vs-2022)

ASP.NET Core can serve your React SPA and provide APIs. Let me show you several approaches:

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Browser (Client)            │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│     React SPA (CSR)                 │
│     ├── Routes (React Router)       │
│     ├── Components                  │
│     └── API Calls (fetch/axios)     │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
               ↓ HTTP/JSON
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│      ASP.NET Core Server             │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Static File Hosting (React)      │
│     └── wwwroot/                     │
│  2. API Controllers                  │
│     └── /api/books, /api/users       │
│  3. Authentication/Authorization     │
│  4. Database Access (EF Core)        │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Approach 1: Serve React Build from wwwroot

### Setup ASP.NET Core

Create a new Web API project:
```bash
dotnet new webapi -n BookLibraryAPI
cd BookLibraryAPI
```

### Configure Program.cs

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services
builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();
builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen();

// Add CORS for development
builder.Services.AddCors(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("ReactApp", policy =>
    {
        policy.WithOrigins("http://localhost:5173")  // Vite default port
              .AllowAnyHeader()
              .AllowAnyMethod();
    });
});

var app = builder.Build();

// Configure pipeline
if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
    app.UseCors("ReactApp");  // Development CORS
}

app.UseDefaultFiles();  // Serve index.html as default
app.UseStaticFiles();   // Serve static files from wwwroot

app.UseRouting();
app.UseAuthorization();

// Map API controllers
app.MapControllers();

// Fallback to index.html for client-side routing
app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html");

app.Run();
```

### Create API Controller

`Controllers/BooksController.cs`:
```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace BookLibraryAPI.Controllers;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class BooksController : ControllerBase
{
    private static List<Book> _books = new()
    {
        new() { Id = 1, Title = "Clean Code", Author = "Robert Martin", Year = 2008 },
        new() { Id = 2, Title = "The Pragmatic Programmer", Author = "Andy Hunt", Year = 1999 }
    };

    [HttpGet]
    public ActionResult<IEnumerable<Book>> GetBooks()
    {
        return Ok(_books);
    }

    [HttpGet("{id}")]
    public ActionResult<Book> GetBook(int id)
    {
        var book = _books.FirstOrDefault(b => b.Id == id);
        if (book == null) return NotFound();
        return Ok(book);
    }

    [HttpPost]
    public ActionResult<Book> CreateBook(Book book)
    {
        book.Id = _books.Max(b => b.Id) + 1;
        _books.Add(book);
        return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetBook), new { id = book.Id }, book);
    }

    [HttpPut("{id}")]
    public IActionResult UpdateBook(int id, Book book)
    {
        var existing = _books.FirstOrDefault(b => b.Id == id);
        if (existing == null) return NotFound();
        
        existing.Title = book.Title;
        existing.Author = book.Author;
        existing.Year = book.Year;
        
        return NoContent();
    }

    [HttpDelete("{id}")]
    public IActionResult DeleteBook(int id)
    {
        var book = _books.FirstOrDefault(b => b.Id == id);
        if (book == null) return NotFound();
        
        _books.Remove(book);
        return NoContent();
    }
}

public class Book
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public string Author { get; set; } = "";
    public int Year { get; set; }
}
```

### React App Setup (Vite)

Create React app in a separate folder:
```bash
npm create vite@latest book-library-react -- --template react-ts
cd book-library-react
npm install
npm install axios react-router-dom
```

### React API Service

`src/services/bookService.ts`:
```typescript
import axios from 'axios';

// Development vs Production API URL
const API_BASE = import.meta.env.DEV 
  ? 'http://localhost:5000/api'  // ASP.NET Core dev server
  : '/api';  // Production: same origin

const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: API_BASE,
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  }
});

export interface Book {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  author: string;
  year: number;
}

export const bookService = {
  getAll: () => api.get<Book[]>('/books'),
  getById: (id: number) => api.get<Book>(`/books/${id}`),
  create: (book: Omit<Book, 'id'>) => api.post<Book>('/books', book),
  update: (id: number, book: Book) => api.put(`/books/${id}`, book),
  delete: (id: number) => api.delete(`/books/${id}`)
};
```

### Build React for Production

In `vite.config.ts`:
```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  build: {
    outDir: '../BookLibraryAPI/wwwroot',  // Build to ASP.NET wwwroot
    emptyOutDir: true
  }
})
```

Build command:
```bash
npm run build
```

## Approach 2: Development with Proxy

For development, run both servers separately:

### ASP.NET Core (Backend)
```bash
cd BookLibraryAPI
dotnet run  # Runs on http://localhost:5000
```

### React Dev Server with Proxy
In React's `vite.config.ts`:
```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  server: {
    proxy: {
      '/api': {
        target: 'http://localhost:5000',
        changeOrigin: true
      }
    }
  }
})
```

Run React:
```bash
npm run dev  # Runs on http://localhost:5173
```

## Approach 3: ASP.NET Core SPA Middleware

For tighter integration, use the SPA middleware:

```csharp
// Program.cs
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddSpaStaticFiles(configuration =>
{
    configuration.RootPath = "ClientApp/dist";  // Your React build output
});

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseStaticFiles();
app.UseSpaStaticFiles();

app.UseRouting();

app.MapControllers();

app.UseSpa(spa =>
{
    spa.Options.SourcePath = "ClientApp";
    
    if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
    {
        // Proxy to React dev server
        spa.UseProxyToSpaDevelopmentServer("http://localhost:5173");
        
        // OR start React dev server automatically
        // spa.UseReactDevelopmentServer(npmScript: "dev");
    }
});

app.Run();
```

## Approach 4: Next.js with ASP.NET Core

If using Next.js with static export:

`next.config.js`:
```javascript
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  output: 'export',
  distDir: '../BookLibraryAPI/wwwroot',
  trailingSlash: true,
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

## Deployment Structure

```
BookLibraryAPI/
├── Controllers/
│   └── BooksController.cs     # API endpoints
├── wwwroot/                    # React build output
│   ├── index.html              # SPA entry point
│   ├── assets/                 # JS/CSS bundles
│   │   ├── index-abc123.js
│   │   └── index-def456.css
│   └── favicon.ico
├── Program.cs
└── BookLibraryAPI.csproj
```

## Benefits of This Approach

1. **Single Deployment**: One server hosts both frontend and API
2. **No CORS Issues**: Same origin for production
3. **Authentication**: Share ASP.NET Core's auth cookies/tokens
4. **Performance**: Static files served efficiently
5. **SEO Option**: Can pre-render or use Razor for specific pages

## Docker Deployment Example

```dockerfile
# Build React
FROM node:18 AS react-build
WORKDIR /app
COPY book-library-react/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY book-library-react/ ./
RUN npm run build

# Build .NET
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0 AS dotnet-build
WORKDIR /app
COPY BookLibraryAPI/*.csproj ./
RUN dotnet restore
COPY BookLibraryAPI/ ./
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o out

# Runtime
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=dotnet-build /app/out ./
COPY --from=react-build /app/dist ./wwwroot
EXPOSE 80
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "BookLibraryAPI.dll"]
```

## Quick Start Script

Create a `setup.sh`:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Create ASP.NET Core API
dotnet new webapi -n BookLibraryAPI
cd BookLibraryAPI

# Create React app
npm create vite@latest ClientApp -- --template react-ts
cd ClientApp
npm install
npm install axios react-router-dom

# Configure build output to wwwroot
echo "Update vite.config.ts to output to ../wwwroot"

# Return to root
cd ../..
```

This setup gives you:
- **Development**: Hot reload for both React and C#
- **Production**: Optimized static files served by ASP.NET Core
- **API**: RESTful endpoints at `/api/*`
- **Routing**: Client-side routing with fallback to index.html
